correctness.rationale: Positive increments force at most one tight constraint from each pair {x_i=0,S_i=B_i}, while each binary selection yields a feasible vertex; hence all vertices are enumerated. The last-positive-index norm bound and case split show unique diametral pair B_n e_n and B_(n-1)e_(n-1). For unit increments the next-largest sum of squares among index-gap compositions is (n-2)^2+1, attained by the two specified vertices (coincident at n=3). Contrasting other-pair norm bounds proves the strict second layer. Exact enumeration checked six unit dimensions and fifteen rational increment configurations, supplementary only.
